Contributor.description:
Represents a contributor to the resource.

Contributors must have a 'contributor_type', either 'Person' or 'Organization', and
one of the 'name' fields: either 'given_name' and 'family_name' (for a person), or 'name' (for an organization or a person).

The 'contributor_role' field takes values from the DataCite and CRediT contributor
roles vocabularies. For more information on these resources and choosing
appropriate roles, please see the following links:

DataCite contributor roles: [https://support.datacite.org/docs/datacite-metadata-schema-v44-recommended-and-optional-properties#7a-contributortype](https://support.datacite.org/docs/datacite-metadata-schema-v44-recommended-and-optional-properties#7a-contributortype)

CRediT contributor role taxonomy: [https://credit.niso.org](https://credit.niso.org).

affiliations.description: List of organizations with which the contributor is affiliated. For contributors that represent an organization, this may be a parent organization (e.g. KBase, US DOE; Arkin lab, LBNL).

contributor_id.description: Persistent unique identifier for the contributor; this might be an ORCID for an individual, or a ROR ID for an organization.

contributor_roles.description: List of roles played by the contributor when working on the resource.

family_name.description: The family name(s) of the contributor.

given_name.description: The given name(s) of the contributor.

name.description: Contributor name. For organizations, this should be the full (unabbreviated) name; can also be used for a person if the given name/family name format is not applicable.

Contributor.title: Contributor

ContributorRole.description: The type of contribution made by a contributor.
ContributorRole.title: ContributorRole

ContributorType.description: The type of contributor being represented.
ContributorType.title: ContributorType

CreditMetadata.description:
Represents the credit metadata associated with an object.

In the following documentation, 'resource' is used to refer to the object
that the CM pertains to, for example, a KBase Workspace object; a
sample from NMDC or ESS-DIVE; sequence data from IMG.

The 'resource_type' field takes values from the ResourceType enum, which combines
the [DataCite resourceTypeGeneral](https://datacite-metadata-schema.readthedocs.io/en/4.7/appendices/appendix-1/resourceTypeGeneral/)
vocabulary with the resource types used by Commonmeta, Crossref, and OSTI. A free
text description of the resource type can be supplied in 'resource_type_detail'.

One or more licenses may be supplied. Each license may be given as an URL pointing to licensing information for
the resource, or using an SPDX license identifier from the list maintained at [https://spdx.org/licenses](https://spdx.org/licenses).

Required fields are:
- identifier
- resource_type
- versioning information: if the resource does not have an explicit version number,
one or more dates should be supplied: ideally the date of resource publication and
the last update (if applicable).
- contributors (one or more required)
- titles (one or more required)
- meta

The resource_type field is required; if no value is supplied, it is populated
with 'dataset'.

comment.description: List of strings of freeform text providing extra information about this credit metadata.
examples: This comment adds a lot of extra value!

content_url.description: The URL of the content of the resource.

contributors.description: A list of people and/or organizations who contributed to the resource.

dates.description: A list of relevant lifecycle events for the resource. Note that these dates apply only to the resource itself, and not to the creation or update of the credit metadata record for the resource.

descriptions.description: A brief description or abstract for the resource being represented.

identifier.description: Resolvable persistent unique identifier for the resource. Should be in the format <database name>:<identifier within database>.

language.description: The primary language of the resource, using the appropriate IETF BCP-47 notation.

license.description:
Usage licenses or rights statements for the resource. For each license, use one of the SPDX license identifiers or provide a link to the license text if no SPDX ID is available.

Supply more than one license if different licenses apply to different versions or uses of the resource (see 'applies_to'), or if the resource is available under a choice of licenses.

meta.description: Metadata for this credit information, including submitter, schema version, and timestamp.

publisher.description: The publisher of the resource. For a dataset, this is the repository where it is stored.

related_identifiers.description: Other resolvable persistent unique IDs related to the resource.

resource_type.description: The broad type of the resource. Defaults to 'dataset'.

titles.description: One or more titles for the resource.

version.description: The version of the resource. This must be an absolute version, not a relative version like 'latest'.

CreditMetadata.title: CreditMetadata

DataSource.description: Source of any kind of data.

access_timestamp.description: Unix timestamp for when the data was retrieved from that source.

source_data_updated.description: The date when the data source was last updated, if available.

source_name.description: Where the data was retrieved from.

source_url.description: URL from whence data was retrieved.

DataSource.title: DataSource

Description.description: Textual information about the resource being represented.

description_text.description: The text content of the informational element.
examples: This is the most interesting dataset ever to earn a DOI.

description_type.description: The type of text being represented.

Description.title: Description

DescriptionType.description: The type of text being represented.
DescriptionType.title: DescriptionType

EventDate.description:
Represents an event in the lifecycle of a resource and the date it occurred on.

See [DataCite documentation on date events](https://support.datacite.org/docs/datacite-metadata-schema-v44-recommended-and-optional-properties#8-date) for more information on the events.

date.description:
The date associated with the event. The date may be in the format YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD, or an ISO 8601 date-time (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssTZD).

A date range may be given using the [RKMS-ISO8601](https://www.ukoln.ac.uk/metadata/dcmi/collection-RKMS-ISO8601/) notation, e.g. 2020-01-01/2020-06-30. The start of the range may be 'unknown'; the end may be 'unknown' or 'open'. Date ranges are useful for 'collected', 'coverage', and 'valid' events.

event.description: The nature of the resource-related event that occurred on that date.

event_information.description: Free text information about the event or date.
examples: Samples collected during the 2019 field season.

EventDate.title: EventDate

EventType.description: The type of date being represented.
EventType.title: EventType

FundingReference.description:
Represents a funding source for a resource, including the funding body and the grant awarded.

One (or more) of the fields 'grant_id', 'grant_url', or 'funder.organization_name' is required; others are optional.

Recommended resources for organization identifiers include:
  - [Research Organization Registry](http://ror.org)
  - [International Standard Name Identifier](https://isni.org)
  - [Crossref Funder Registry](https://www.crossref.org/services/funder-registry/) (to be subsumed into ROR)

Some organizations may have a digital object identifier (DOI).

funder.description: The funder for the grant or award.

grant_id.description: Code for the grant, assigned by the funder.

examples: Metagenomic analysis of the rhizosphere of three biofuel crops at the KBS intensive site

FundingReference.title: FundingReference

License.description:
License or rights information for the resource.

One (or more) of 'id', 'url', or 'name' is required.

id.description: String representing the license, from the [SPDX license identifiers](https://spdx.org/licenses/).

name.description: Full name of the license or a rights statement, if no SPDX identifier is available. Include version information if applicable.

License.title: License

Metadata.description: Metadata for the credit metadata, including the schema version used, who submitted it, and the date of submission. When the credit metadata for a resource is added or updated, this additional metadata must be provided along with the credit information.

credit_metadata_schema_version.description: The version of the credit metadata schema used.

credit_metadata_source.description: Information about where the credit metadata was sourced from.

saved_by.description: PID for the user who added this entry.

timestamp.description: Unix timestamp for the addition of this set of credit metadata.

Metadata.title: Metadata

Organization.description:
Represents an organization.

Recommended resources for organization identifiers include:
  - [Research Organization Registry](http://ror.org)
  - [International Standard Name Identifier](https://isni.org)
  - [Crossref Funder Registry](https://www.crossref.org/services/funder-registry/) (to be subsumed into ROR)

For example, the US DOE would be entered as:
  organization_name: United States Department of Energy
  organization_id:   ROR:01bj3aw27

organization_id.description: Persistent unique identifier for the organization in the format <database name>:<identifier within database>.

organization_name.description: Common name of the organization; use the name recommended by ROR if possible.

Organization.title: Organization

PermanentID.description:
Represents a persistent unique identifier for an entity and its relationship to some other entity.

The 'id' field and 'relationship_type' fields are required.

The values in the 'relationship_type' field come from controlled vocabularies maintained by DataCite and Crossref. See the documentation links below for more details.

[DataCite relation types](https://support.datacite.org/docs/datacite-metadata-schema-v44-recommended-and-optional-properties#12b-relationtype)

[Crossref relation types](https://www.crossref.org/documentation/schema-library/markup-guide-metadata-segments/relationships/)

examples: This data analysis workflow demonstrates how to process a metagenome to identify viruses using VirSorter. Then, provides taxonomic classification using vConTACT2.

id.description: Persistent unique ID for an entity. Should be in the format <database name>:<identifier within database>.

relationship_type.description: The relationship between the ID and some other entity. For example, when a PermanentID class is used to represent objects in the CreditMetadata field 'related_identifiers', the 'relationship_type' field captures the relationship between the resource being registered and this ID.

relationship_type_information.description: Free text further describing the relationship, e.g. when the relationship type is 'other'.
examples: Raw reads used to generate the assembly.

PermanentID.title: PermanentID

RelationshipType.description: The relationship between two entities. For example, when a PermanentID class is used to represent objects in the CreditMetadata field 'related_identifiers', the 'relationship_type' field captures the relationship between the resource being registered (A) and this ID (B).
RelationshipType.title: RelationshipType

ResourceType.description:
The type of resource being represented.

Values combine the [DataCite resourceTypeGeneral](https://datacite-metadata-schema.readthedocs.io/en/4.7/appendices/appendix-1/resourceTypeGeneral/) vocabulary (v4.7) with the resource types used by [Commonmeta](https://docs.commonmeta.org), Crossref, and OSTI. Where a resource type exists in DataCite, the DataCite term is used.
ResourceType.title: ResourceType

Title.description:
Represents the title or name of a resource, the type of that title, and the language used (if appropriate).

The 'title' field is required; 'title_type' is only necessary if the text is not the primary title.

language.description: The language in which the title is written, using the appropriate IETF BCP-47 notation.

title.description: A string used as a title for a resource.

title_type.description: A descriptor for the title for cases where the contents of the 'title' field is not the primary name or title.

Title.title: Title

TitleType.description: The type of title being represented.
TitleType.title: TitleType
